sections.title: The letter name
paragraphs: The letter is named (Qu) /kuː/. Its main sound appears in (Quelle) /ˈkvɛlə/, which means source or spring. This letter has two sounds in German.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof. Release the air cleanly, then place your top teeth against your lower lip. Blow air through to make a buzzing friction. Touch your throat to feel it shake. For the second sound, release only the air burst without the lip buzz. Keep your throat quiet.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: The letter almost always pairs with another letter in native words. This common pair makes the first sound, as in (Quatsch) /kvatʃ/. It also makes this sound in the middle of words, as in (Bequem) /bəˈkveːm/. In French loanwords, the letter makes only the single click sound. You hear this sound at the start of (Quiche) /kiːʃ/ and inside (Bouquet) /buˈkeː/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not round your lips into a smooth glide like in the English word quick. In German, bring your lower lip against your upper teeth. You must feel a clear buzzing friction like the sound in vine. Also do not add this buzz to French loanwords.
